# The Problem

There are three language servers for R:
[languageserver](https://github.com/REditorSupport/languageserver),
[Ark](https://github.com/posit-dev/ark), and Arity. languageserver is a mature R
package that runs in an R session. Ark embeds its language server in an R kernel
and powers R support in Positron. Arity, meanwhile, is a standalone language
server that works without an R session or Jupyter kernel. Adapting Ark to
Arity's design would have required extracting the server and replacing its
dependencies on the R runtime, which is what motivated the development of Arity.

Yet Arity still has limitations that affect package development. It can, for
instance, misinterpret shared roxygen documentation, miss undocumented
parameters, and handle references and call hierarchy inconsistently. Renaming
can also produce invalid R syntax, for example when a function is used as an
infix operator.

Arity also needs better support for dependencies that are not installed locally.
It provides signatures and help for installed packages, but only exported names
for others. Richer metadata would provide that assistance without installation
and enable linting of deprecated and defunct functions. The editor and
command-line interface (CLI) also need to share cached metadata when downloads
are disabled.
